hazards.control: Pressure test before opening to the well; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Stay clear of the coil path, the gooseneck, and flowback iron under flow.

name: Quad BOP (blind, shear, slip, pipe rams)
function: The blowout preventer of the coiled tubing stack: four ram sets in one block body, hydraulically closed, that seal the well with the coil in place, hold the coil, cut it, or seal the open bore.

tabs.overview: From the top: blind rams seal the open bore with no coil in it; shear rams cut the coil and leave the cut open for circulation; slip rams grip the coil against movement; pipe rams seal around the coil (S24). Equalizing and kill ports let pressure be balanced across rams and fluid pumped below them. Tie-rod actuators on both sides of each ram level; manual locks on some designs.
tabs.engineering: Working pressure 10,000 psi common (S24); ram inserts sized to the coil; bore matched to the BHA.
tabs.safety: Rams are function-tested before the job and pressure-tested on the stack; the shear ram is the last resort and is only closed with the coil stopped.
tabs.evidence: Public coiled tubing pressure control guide (S24), API RP 16ST and API RP 5C7 scope (S23, S26), field practice (S9).

standards.paraphrase: Ram configuration, ratings, and testing for coiled tubing BOPs.
